When the Neutrinos Leave: Decoupling History and the Threshold for Primordial Black Hole Formation

Jeromie Beasley

31 October 2026 (version 3)

AI-assisted. The ideas and research direction are the author’s; AI tools (Claude, Anthropic) were used for literature search, computation, drafting and typesetting. The numbers come from the scripts, run logs and outputs printed in Appendix B. The simulations are runs of S. McCormick’s public code on a cloud computer, not experiments.

Abstract

McCormick has shown that neutrinos which stream freely out of a collapsing overdensity raise the threshold for primordial black hole formation, by about 0.235Rν in the linear compaction, and that the effect fades when the neutrinos decouple gradually. This paper asks what sets that fading. First, the neutrino collision operator is read exactly as a cut between what is kept and what streams. All of its non-normality, 18∥[L,L*]∥2=κ2k2/3, lies on the single link between density and flux. With separate rates for flux and shear it is k2κ12/3+4k215(κ2−κ1)2, and the weight across the cut equals the sound speed, EB=k/3. Second, McCormick’s own code is run on five cases outside his paper, with every prediction and kill line written down before the runs. A broad profile that collapses near ϵ≈7–9 keeps the same share of the neutrino effect as a Gaussian that collapses near ϵ≈4, or less (G=0.181 and 0.045 against 0.190 and 0.063), so the collapse time alone does not set the clock. A steeper decoupling history, κ/H=(ϵdec/ϵ)6, gives G=0.648, 0.317 and 0.154 at ϵdec=1, 2 and 3, against 0.683, 0.431 and about 0.30 for the standard history: how the neutrinos leave matters, not only when. The steep-history thresholds are unchanged by a tenfold higher collision-rate cap and by a finer grid. One reading survives every run: the memory of the kept sector, the population the density keeps under the decoupling operator, read mostly at the first compaction maximum. With one weight fitted to McCormick’s curve and then frozen, it predicted 0.663, 0.246 and 0.118 before the runs, all within the kill line of 0.08; a history-blind rule fails at ϵdec=3 by 0.146. Third, the memory has a location. Two neutrino states with the same density, flux and anisotropic stress, differing only in finer angular structure, give later density, flux and stress that differ by several per cent, when the difference is set at or after decoupling; set deep in the coupled era it is erased, by the factor exp[−ϵdecn/(nτsn)]. An exact block elimination puts the whole effect in one hidden-source term, and the kept population obeys (Ȧ)2≤4EBA(1−A). A closure on density, flux and stress cannot carry this memory. The algebraic identities, the counterexample and the verdict arithmetic are written in Lean for machine checking (Appendix C). Four further tests are stated for the e± annihilation epoch and for collision terms beyond relaxation time.

The question

Primordial black holes heavier than about 106M⊙ form while the neutrinos, which carry 41–49% of the radiation, stop scattering and stream freely. McCormick evolved these neutrinos with their angle-resolved transport equation inside spherical general relativity and found that free streaming makes collapse harder [1]. The threshold on the linear compaction Cl, which sets abundance, rises by ΔCl,c/Cl,c≃0.235Rν, and the threshold δc on the compaction peak rises by ≃0.15Rν. For Gaussian fluctuations a perfect-fluid collapse probability β becomes about β1.18 above 6×105M⊙.

He also ran gradual decoupling, with collision rate κ=H(ϵdec/ϵ)3, where ϵ=1/(aHrm) is the Hubble radius in units of the perturbation size. Write G for the share of the instantaneous free-streaming shift that survives: G=δc−δcfluidδcinst−δcfluid. His Table II gives G= 0.959, 0.867, 0.683, 0.431, 0.190 and 0.063 at ϵdec= 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 and 8. He notes that linear theory gives estimates of opposite sign and “does not determine which diagnostic, if any, predicts the nonlinear threshold” [1, Sec. IV C].

Two questions follow and are answered here. What in the neutrino transport operator carries the effect (Section 2)? And which clock, and which part of the decoupling history, sets G (Sections 3–5)?

The collision operator as a cut

For one Fourier mode k, the linearised neutrino intensity in McCormick’s relaxation model evolves under ∂tf=Lf,L=A+D,A=−ikμ,D=−κ(I−P), where μ is the cosine of the angle to the wave vector and P projects onto the isotropic part. Free streaming A is anti-Hermitian. Collisions D are Hermitian, conserve the isotropic part (the neutrino energy in the plasma frame) and remove the flux, which goes to the plasma. In the normalised Legendre basis |ℓ⟩, streaming couples only neighbours, ⟨ℓ+1|μ|ℓ⟩=cℓ=(ℓ+1)/(2ℓ+1)(2ℓ+3), so the operator lives on a chain ℓ=0,1,2,… (Figure 1).

Non-normality is connection energy.

For Hermitian D and anti-Hermitian A, [L,L*]=2[A,D], and for diagonal D, [A,D]ij=Aij(Dj−Di). Hence 18∥[L,L*]∥F2=∑links ℓ→ℓ+1k2cℓ2(Dℓ+1−Dℓ)2. This is the scalar case of the identity in [3]: the self-commutator energy of a transport operator is the energy of its Hermitian field failing to be parallel along the links [derived; Appendix A.1]. With one rate, only the link 0→1 has a jump, so 18∥[L,L*]∥F2=κ2k23[derived; checked to 1e-12, I1]. All the non-normality of the single-rate model lies on the link between density and flux, the same channel as the momentum drag κq in McCormick’s plasma equation [1, Eq. (6)].

Beyond relaxation time.

Let the flux relax at κ1 (momentum transfer) and shear and higher moments at κ2. Then two links carry jumps: 18∥[L,L*]∥F2=k2κ123+4k215(κ2−κ1)2[derived; checked, I2]. The energy is stationary in κ2 at κ2=κ1. If neutrino–neutrino scattering damps shear but not flux, with rates relative to e± scattering of 1.5 for νe and 7 for νμ,τ, the shear link carries 64% and 97.5% of the non-normality [computed, under those assumed ratios].

The weight across the cut is the sound speed.

With H=kμ the weight between kept and streaming parts is EB=∥PH(I−P)∥2=k2c02=k2/3, so EB=k/3=csk, the radiation sound speed [4] [derived; I3]. A rate bound built on EB therefore sees the root-mean-square streaming speed 1/3, not the light-speed front that empties the overdensity [5].

The kept sector, exactly.

The isotropic part has the closed propagator ⟨0|(s−L)−1|0⟩=g1−κg,g=1karctanks+κ[derived; checked, I4]. The two-moment truncation, keeping ℓ=0,1, has eigenvalues −κ/2±κ2/4−k2/3, which merge at κ=2k/3 [derived; I5]. This exceptional point belongs to the truncation. With 200 moments the least-damped mode turns real only at κ≈0.646k, and in relaxation kinetic theory the hydrodynamic poles meet a branch cut instead [8,9] [computed].

New runs of McCormick’s code

The code [2] was run unchanged except for one copied file in which the decoupling exponent n in κ=H(ϵdec/ϵ)n is an input. Pure radiation, Rν=0.409, N=400 cells, Nμ=32 angle bins, ϵ0=0.1, as in his Table II. A reproduction run at δ=0.5109 with n=3, ϵdec=2 forms a black hole, inside his published bracket (0.51074,0.51109) [measured; Appendix B.4]. For the steep history, κ/H was capped at 5×105, the stiffness his own ϵdec=8 runs reach at ϵ0. At that cap deviations from isotropy are of relative order H/κ≤2×10−6, the same estimate McCormick uses for his switch to transport [1, Sec. III].

For every test below each prediction and its kill condition were written before the runs (Appendix B.3). The threshold search runs two points per round; a run that neither collapses nor disperses by the end time, or that stops on an error, never moves the bracket, is retried once with a longer end time and is reported if still undecided. No point in any run below was undecided.

Test A: a profile that collapses late.

The broad profile α=0.3 is decided near ϵ≈7–9, against ϵ≈4 for the Gaussian. Its thresholds are δcfluid=0.44805 and δcinst=0.47747 [2]. With n=3:

δc G (broad) G (Gaussian, [1])
ϵdec=4 0.45337±0.00013 0.181±0.004 0.190
ϵdec=8 0.44938±0.00012 0.045±0.004 0.063

The broad profile keeps the same share of the neutrino effect as the Gaussian or less (29% less at ϵdec=8), although it collapses about twice as late (Figure 2) [measured]. A clock tied to the collapse time would have raised G; it fell. Because the test changes the profile shape together with the collapse time, it shows that the collapse time alone does not set the clock; it does not by itself separate the two, and it does not fix which earlier epoch does.

Tests B, C and D: a steeper decoupling history.

Gaussian profile, κ/H=(ϵdec/ϵ)6:

δc G (n=6) G (n=3, [1])
C: ϵdec=1 0.51756±0.00019 0.648±0.006 0.683
B: ϵdec=2 0.50743±0.00011 0.317±0.004 0.431
D: ϵdec=3 0.50245±0.00019 0.154±0.006 ≈0.30

[measured]. The n=3 value at ϵdec=3 lies between McCormick’s 0.431 and 0.190 at 2 and 4. A neutrino population that decouples more abruptly, but by the same nominal time, keeps less of its effect, and the gap widens with ϵdec. The history matters, not only its end point.

Numerical controls.

Test B was repeated with the rate cap raised tenfold, to 5×106, and on a finer grid, N=600 cells and Nμ=48 angle bins. The thresholds are δc=0.50740±0.00011 and 0.50751±0.00006, shifts of −0.00003 and +0.00008 against the pre-registered tolerance of 0.0005 [measured]. The cap acts only while the neutrinos are tightly coupled: the uncapped rate starts at (ϵdec/ϵ0)6 and falls below the cap at ϵ≈0.11, 0.22 and 0.34 for ϵdec=1, 2 and 3. The cap control was run at ϵdec=2 only; at ϵdec=1 and 3 it is untested.

What does not set the threshold

Each reading below was tested against numbers. Only the last two were tested against runs set up for them in advance; the first three were tested against McCormick’s published curve.

  1. The first maximum of linear theory. The linear density contrast at its first maximum (ϵ≈1.7) reproduces the instantaneous shift (centre factor 0.944, as McCormick finds). Under gradual decoupling the share it keeps is 0.86, 0.59, 0.19, −0.05, −0.02 and 0.00, a largest error of 0.50. Decoupling after ϵ≈1.7 is nearly invisible to it, yet still moves the nonlinear threshold [computed].

  2. A sharp wall, and rate ratios. Treat the two-moment exceptional point, crossed at ϵEP=0.811ϵdec3/4 for krm=2, as a wall, or use the parameter-free escape fractions k/(k+κ), e−κ/k and 1−e−k/κ. Averaging each over two windows, with two weightings and two scales, gives 32 combinations. The wall variants miss by 0.14 or more. With the window starting at horizon entry, every combination misses by 0.17 or more. One combination, e−κ/k averaged from ϵ0, comes within 0.077; selected from 32, it is not counted. On Test B, which it never saw, it predicts 0.513 against 0.317 [computed; measured].

  3. Diffusive escape. Diffusion with D=1/(3σ) from the conformal rate σ=ϵdec3/τ4, combined in series with streaming at the collapse time ϵ*, gives G=1/[1+15(ϵdec/ϵ*)3/2]. With ϵ*=4 it matches McCormick’s curve to 0.02, but it was built after seeing that curve, and a free fit of its exponent gives 1.61±0.03 rather than 3/2. Test A with ϵ*=7–9 predicted 0.37–0.47 and 0.17–0.24, and Test B predicted 0.62. Both are excluded [measured].

  4. History-blind. If only ϵdec mattered, Tests B and D would give 0.431 and about 0.30. They give 0.317 and 0.154; Test D misses by 0.146 against a kill line of 0.08 [measured].

What survives: the memory of the kept sector

The reading that survives treats the isotropic part as a kept sector and asks how much of it the decoupling operator keeps [4]. Start a mode in |0⟩ at τ0=0.02 and evolve it under ∂τv=−(ikμ+aκ(τ)(I−P))v, with aκ=ϵdecn/τn+1. Let A(τ) be the population left in |0⟩, averaged over the Gaussian profile with weights k2e−k2/2. Define g(ϵ*)=1−Aϵdec(ϵ*)1−Ainst(ϵ*), the share of the kept sector’s loss that has happened by the readout time ϵ*.

With no fitted number, read at the first compaction maximum ϵ*=1.7, it gives 0.941, 0.860, 0.671, 0.344, 0.087 and 0.013 against McCormick’s G. That is within 0.02 for ϵdec≤1, with a largest error of 0.103, just outside the 0.10 bar set for it in advance [computed]. McCormick’s own curve passes G=12 at ϵdec≈1.67, within 3% of the first maximum: the neutrinos must be decoupled by then for half the effect to survive.

The late shortfall says the collapse is still listening after the first maximum. Mixing the two epochs McCormick’s numbers single out, g2=wg(1.7)+(1−w)g(4.0), with one weight fitted to his curve, w=0.89, gives a largest error of 0.022 [fit]. The form is not unique: with the scale fixed at krm=2 the single-epoch reading misses by 0.093, and the best single readout epoch, ϵ*=1.87, by 0.065. Its weight does not carry over between weightings: the same w with the scale fixed at krm=2 misses by 0.115, outside the 0.10 bar declared for that check [computed]. The form is a fitted shape with a stated sensitivity, not a derived law.

The test is what that fitted form says about histories it never saw. All its n=6 values were computed in one file dated 13:47 on 30 October, before any n=6 run, and were not refitted afterwards:

predicted measured miss history-blind miss
C: ϵdec=1 0.663 0.648 0.014 0.683 0.035
B: ϵdec=2 0.246 0.317 0.071 0.431 0.114
D: ϵdec=3 0.118 0.154 0.037 ≈0.30 0.146

Every miss of the memory form lies inside the kill line of 0.08 set before its run; the history-blind rule fails at ϵdec=3 (Figures 3 and 4) [measured]. At ϵdec=2 and 3 the form falls below the measurement: it counts slightly too much of the early erasure. Test C was set where the two rules nearly agree, as a survival check; Test D was set where they separate. A readout window set by the neutrino flux and the enclosed mass between first maximum and apparent horizon, as McCormick suggests [1, Sec. IV C], is the natural next object. It is untested.

Where the memory sits

A fluid closure carries the density, the flux and the anisotropic stress, the moments ℓ=0,1,2. The memory form of Section 5 says the threshold depends on how the kept sector was emptied. The question here is whether that history can sit in moments a closure does not carry.

Exact elimination of the hidden moments.

Split v=(a,h) with a=v0 and h=(v1,v2,…). In the relaxation model every hidden moment is damped at the same rate, so the collision term on the hidden block is σ(τ) times the identity and commutes with streaming. The hidden propagator is therefore exact in closed form, UQ(t,r)=e−[Σ(t)−Σ(r)]e−ik(t−r)MQQ,Σ(τ)=−ϵdecnnτn,Σ′=σ, and eliminating h gives one equation for the kept amplitude, ȧ(t)=S(t)−k2∫stK(t,r)a(r)dr,K=c02[UQ(t,r)]11,S=−ikc0[UQ(t,s)h(s)]1 [derived; Appendix A.5]. The kernel K is the memory; the source S is everything the hidden moments held at time s.

The matched pair.

Take two states with the same (v0,v1,v2)=(1,0.2,0.1), differing only by ±0.05 in v3 (or v4), scaled by one constant to unit norm. Both are positive angular distributions (f(μ)≥0.50). Their kept amplitudes start equal, so their difference obeys the equation above driven only by S of the hidden difference. Both are evolved under the same history, ϵdec=0.5, with the planting time τs scanned across decoupling. The readout is the profile-weighted change in (v0,v1,v2), relative to its size, Rret; the witness is on if Rret>10−3. Every on/off call was written down before the run, from the survival factor of the hidden block, exp[−ϵdecn/(nτsn)], and the leakage (k/σ)ℓ through damped rungs (Appendix B.14).

τs/ϵdec n=3, ℓ=3 n=3, ℓ=4 n=6, ℓ=3 n=6, ℓ=4
0.1 7×10−15 5×10−19 8×10−24 5×10−31
0.25 6×10−10 6×10−11 2×10−15 7×10−20
0.5 8.6×𝟏𝟎−𝟑 7.9×𝟏𝟎−𝟑 3×10−6 3×10−6
1 0.081 0.074 0.094 0.086
2 0.095 0.085 0.098 0.088

Rret at τ=4; bold entries are on [computed]. Every call came out as predicted. The survival law is quantitative: for n=3 the ratio of the entries at 0.5 and 1 is 0.106 against e−8/3/e−1/3=0.097, and for n=6 at 0.5 the law gives 1.4×10−6 against 1.6×10−6 at τ=1.7. Planted in the retained moments instead, deep in coupling the order is ℓ=1>2>3>4, each rung costing about 10−4≈k/σ; after decoupling all four are of the same size. A hidden difference set at decoupling changes the later density, flux and stress as much as a visible one (Figure 5).

Checks.

Doubling the number of moments, 60→120, and tightening the solver tolerances change every entry by at most 1.4×10−5 of its value. Solving the elimination equation from the closed-form UQ alone, with no solve of the full system, reproduces the full difference to 3×10−7–7×10−7, falling fourfold with each halving of the step; leaving out the kernel misses by 19–234% [computed; Appendix B.14].

A speed limit on the kept population.

Collisions conserve |0⟩ and remove the rest, so ∥v∥ never grows, and streaming links |0⟩ only to |1⟩, with weight kc0=EB. Hence for A=|v0|2 Ȧ2≤4EBA(1−A),EB=k2/3 [derived; Appendix A.6]. On every trajectory computed here the largest value of the ratio is 0.87 [computed]. The bound limits how fast the kept sector can be emptied; it does not set the threshold.

Reading.

A closure on density, flux and stress is exact only for structure set while the neutrinos are tightly coupled. Structure set at or after decoupling survives in the finer angular moments and streams back into the visible ones by several per cent. The memory McCormick’s runs record therefore has a place to live that no fluid closure contains. Whether realistic initial data carry such structure, and how far it moves the nonlinear threshold, are untested: the memory curves of Section 5 start with the hidden moments empty.

Tests for McCormick’s code

  1. The annihilation control. During e± annihilation the plasma sound speed falls to cs=0.519 at T=0.131 MeV, while the neutrinos’ root-mean-square speed stays 1/3. The contest between front and sound, f=(1−cs)/(1−1/3), reaches 1.135 at 1.6×107M⊙ (cs=0.521 there). If the softer plasma enhanced the free-streaming effect, the shift would reach 7.5%, outside McCormick’s envelope of 5.3–6.2%, so that reading already fails. If it reduces it, the shift stays at 5.5–6.3% [computed; reading]. At 1.6×107M⊙ the two readings differ from the unmodified 6.31% by +13.5% and −11.9%. The run McCormick lists as missing, the same transport at fixed Rν with p=e/3 against the full equation of state at 3×106–1.6×107M⊙, would confirm the sign.

  2. Shear against flux. By Section 2, a collision term that damps shear faster than flux puts most of the non-normality on the flux–shear link. Whether the threshold follows the shear rate more than the momentum-transfer rate needs the response itself, not the energy: the energy is stationary at κ2=κ1, but the response need not be. With three moments and k=s=κ1=κ2=1, the kept response is R00=32/37 with ∂R00/∂κ2=−5/1369≠0, while ∂E/∂κ2=0 [derived; Appendix A.7]. The proposed run varies κ2 at fixed κ1 in McCormick’s code and reads the threshold [proposed].

  3. Independence of Rν. The kept-sector form contains no Rν. One run at Rν=0.2, ϵdec=2, n=3 should give the form’s own value, G=0.411, which McCormick’s Rν=0.409 run puts at 0.431 [proposed].

  4. Which mean of the rates. McCormick calibrates his single rate to an energy-group calculation. The arithmetic mean of the group rates reproduces his calibrated decoupling temperatures: 1.62 MeV against 1.6 (e± only), 1.02 MeV against 0.93–1.0 (with νν), and a mass step of 2.53 against 2.5–3. The harmonic and geometric means fail; the mean of squares also passes, so the class of means is identified, not one mean [4] [computed; reading].

Relation to other work

The closest published analogue is bulk viscosity, which raises the threshold roughly in proportion to its strength in full numerical relativity [10]. Free streaming is a second dissipative channel with the same sign. Papanikolaou fixes thresholds at horizon crossing for a time-dependent equation of state, with δc following cs2 [11]. Escrivà ties them to the initial profile and the curvature of the compaction at its peak [12]. Test A is consistent with both: the neutrino clock is set early.

The 2026 thermal-history mass functions through neutrino decoupling and e± annihilation treat neutrinos as part of the fluid [13], so the step McCormick found is absent from them. For supermassive seeds, the μ-distortion bound leaves only heavy-tailed statistics [14], for which McCormick finds that the raised threshold costs a factor 1.2–8 in abundance in his examples [1].

A search of the literature to October 2026 found no other work on thresholds with free-streaming components, on gradual kinetic decoupling in numerical relativity, or on how the threshold depends on when a collision rate switches off. Tests A–D are, as far as that search shows, the first such runs.

Summary

The neutrino collision operator is a cut whose whole non-normality sits on one link, density to flux, with weight equal to the sound speed. McCormick’s code, run on five cases outside his paper, shows that the collapse time alone does not set the neutrino clock, and that the decoupling history changes the threshold, not only its end point. The kept-sector memory, read mostly at the first compaction maximum and fitted once, predicted three histories it had not seen to within 0.071, 0.014 and 0.037, while a history-blind rule failed. The steep-history thresholds do not move with the rate cap or the grid. The memory sits in the angular structure a fluid closure drops: set at or after decoupling, it returns into density, flux and stress; set before, it is erased.

Proofs

A.1 Non-normality is connection energy, for the neutrino chain

Let L=A+D with A*=−A and D*=D. Then L*=D−A, and [L,L*]=(A+D)(D−A)−(D−A)(A+D)=2(AD−DA)=2[A,D]. For diagonal D=diag(Dℓ), [A,D]ij=Aij(Dj−Di). So 18∥[L,L*]∥F2=12∑i≠j|Aij|2(Di−Dj)2. Streaming couples only ℓ and ℓ±1, with |Aℓ,ℓ+1|=kcℓ. Each link appears twice in the ordered sum, which gives ∑ℓk2cℓ2(Dℓ+1−Dℓ)2. With D=(0,−κ1,−κ2,−κ2,…), c02=1/3 and c12=4/15, this is k2κ12/3+4k215(κ2−κ1)2. With κ1=κ2=κ it is κ2k2/3. ▫

A.2 The weight across the cut

PH(I−P) with H=kμ has the single entry ⟨0|kμ|1⟩=kc0, so EB=k2/3. The variance of kμ in the isotropic state is k2⟨μ2⟩=k2/3, the same number. ▫

A.3 The kept-sector propagator

Write u=(s−L)−1|0⟩, so (s+κ+ikμ)u=|0⟩+κPu. Projecting onto |0⟩ with ⟨0|(s+κ+ikμ)−1|0⟩=12∫−11dμ/(s+κ+ikμ)=k−1arctan[k/(s+κ)]=g gives u0=g(1+κu0), so u0=g/(1−κg). ▫

A.4 The truncated exceptional point

On span{|0⟩,|1⟩}, L=(0−ik/3−ik/3−κ), with characteristic polynomial λ2+κλ+k2/3. Its discriminant κ2−4k2/3 vanishes at κ=2k/3, where the matrix is not diagonalisable. ▫

A.5 Exact elimination of the hidden moments

Write ∂τv=−(ikM+σ(τ)Q)v with Q=I−P, and split v=(a,h) along P and Q. Then ȧ=−ikc0h1 and ḣ=−(ikMQQ+σ)h−ikc0ae1. On the hidden block σ(τ)I commutes with MQQ, so the generators at different times commute and the propagator is the product UQ(t,r)=e−∫rtσe−ik(t−r)MQQ, with ∫rtσ=Σ(t)−Σ(r), Σ(τ)=−ϵdecn/(nτn). Variation of constants gives h(t)=UQ(t,s)h(s)−ikc0∫stUQ(t,r)e1a(r)dr; substituting into ȧ gives ȧ(t)=−ikc0[UQ(t,s)h(s)]1−k2c02∫st[UQ(t,r)]11a(r)dr. For two states with equal a(s) the difference Δa obeys the same equation with source S[Δh(s)] and Δa(s)=0; if Δh(s)=0 it vanishes identically. The time-independent case et(X−σI)=e−σtetX is stated in Lean (Appendix C). ▫

A.6 The speed limit on the kept population

With D=−σQ≤0, ddτ∥v∥2=−2σ∥Qv∥2≤0, so ∥v∥≤1 for a unit initial state. Since ⟨0|D=0 and ⟨0|M=c0⟨1|, v̇0=−ikc0v1, and Ȧ=2Re(v‾0v̇0)=2Re(v‾0(−ikc0)v1),|Ȧ|≤2kc0|v0||v1|. With |v1|2≤∥v∥2−|v0|2≤1−A and k2c02=EB, Ȧ2≤4EBA(1−A). The core inequality |2Re(a‾(−ih)b)|≤2|h||a||b| and the corollary under |a|2+|b|2≤1 are stated in Lean (Appendix C). ▫

A.7 Energy stationarity is not response stationarity

Keep three moments, ℓ=0,1,2, with streaming weights c02=1/3, c12=4/15 and rates (0,κ1,κ2). The kept response R00=⟨0|(s+ikM+D)−1|0⟩ is the continued fraction R00=1s+k2c02s+κ1+k2c12s+κ2. At k=s=κ1=1 this is R00(κ2)=(1+13/(2+4/151+κ2))−1, so R00(1)=32/37 and R00′(1)=−5/1369. The energy E=k2κ12/3+4k215(κ2−κ1)2 has ∂E/∂κ2=8k215(κ2−κ1)=0 there. Checked by direct inversion of the 3×3 matrix; stated in Lean (Appendix C). ▫

Evidence: scripts, run logs and outputs

All scripts, run logs and outputs are printed in full in the PDF edition (Appendix B) and included in the code and data archive.

Lean statements

The statements below are written in Lean 4 with Mathlib (v4.34.1) in the repository neutrinos-leave-lean, with a build that replays every proof in the kernel, audits axioms, and confirms that nine false controls are rejected. A statement counts as machine-checked only once that build passes on a recorded commit; until then it carries the grade of its paper proof. Lean checks the finite moment model and the verdict arithmetic. It does not check McCormick’s code, the collapse runs or the numerical witness.

  1. crossLink: |2Re(a‾(−ih)b)|≤2|h||a||b|; crossLink_sq: with A=|a|2, |a|2+|b|2≤1, the square is at most 4|h|2A(1−A) (Appendix A.6).

  2. twoMomentConnectionEnergy: 18∥[L,L*]∥F2=κ2k2/3 for the two-moment L.

  3. splitRateEnergy: 18∥[L,L*]∥F2=k2κ12/3+4k215(κ2−κ1)2 for the three-moment L.

  4. shearCounterexample: R00(1)=32/37, R00′(1)=−5/1369, ∂κ2E=0 at κ2=κ1; with the complex 3×3 resolvent entry equal to the closed form 2(15κ2+17)/(35κ2+39) for κ2>−1 (Appendix A.7).

  5. scalarCollisionPropagator: et(X−σI)=e−σtetX, with generators X−σ(t)I commuting pairwise (Appendix A.5).

  6. testB/C/D_verdict: GB=970/3059, GC=1983/3059, GD=472/3059 against the pre-registered kill lines.
